newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbeks target 1997 4.0 mln tonne grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks target 1997 4.0 mln tonne grain harvest.

text.p: Uzbekistan plans to harvest four million tonnes of grain in 1997, 500,000 tonnes more than last year, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.

"Good weather conditions this year and timely agri-technical work allow us to say the target of four million tonnes of grain is achievable," Zair Latypov, deputy head of the ministry's grain-growing department, told Reuters.
Last year Uzbekistan harvested 3.54 million tonnes of grain.
But Latypov said the government had to reconsider its initial target of 4.5 million tonnes of grain due to lower irrigated areas this year.
He said the area sown to grain totalled 1.49 million hectares in 1997, compared with 1.69 million last year. Irrigated areas totalled one million hectares against 1.19 million hectares last year.
The government was hopeful crop yields this year would be higher than last when farmers harvested an average 2.1 tonnes per hectare, but has given no concrete figures.
Latypov said the harvest campaign started in southern regions of largely desert Uzbekistan several days ago, a week earlier than last year.
The government wants the harvest to be over by the end of June. --Shamil Baigin, tashkent Newsroom, +7 3712 361958
